full_judgment:
Borhanuddin J. This civil appeal by leave is directed against the judgment and order dated 21.11.2001 passed by a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.3987 of 1991  (Dhaka)  Civil Revision Mo.149 of 1990 (Rangpur) making the Rule absolute obtained against the Order No.110 dated. 16.06.1990 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Gaibandha, in Other Suit No.28 of 1959 setting aside the ex-parte decree dated 23.05.1987 as to the land described in 'Uma' schedule and thereupon passing the preliminary decree on 21.06.1988 and finally making the preliminary decree final on 12.03.1990 and also setting aside the order dated 19.03.1990. The learned Assistant Judge while setting aside the decree in the partition suit upon an application filed under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure directed the defendants to pay 11.500/- to the plaintiff within 30(thirty) days from date and in ease of default the application under section. 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure would stand rejected. 

 4. The trial Court decreed the suit on 17.07.1963 except the land of C.S Plot No.247 in 'Gra' schedule. Being aggrieved, the defendant nos.1 and 2 preferred appeal no.175 of 1965 in the Court of learned District Judge, Rangpur. The appellate Court modified the decree of the trial Court upon upholding plaintiffs claim of share in the schedules except lima' schedule described in the plaint. 

 5. Having dissatisfied, plaintiff filed 2nd appeal being no.887 of 1966 before the High Court Division. The High Court Division affirmed the judgment and decree of the appellate Court below as regards the land described in the schedules of the plaint other than the 'lima' schedule and sent back the suit to the trial Court for deciding the dispute of the parties relating to the land described in lima' schedule. The trial Court after receiving the case record fixed the date for pre-emptory hearing. Though several dates were fixed but the defendants did not appear and then the learned Munsif fixed the date for ex-parte hearing on 23.05.1987. On the date fixed, the defendants did not take any step and the learned Munsif upon hearing the plaintiff decreed the suit ex-parte infavour of the plaintiff in respect of the land described in 'Uma' schedule vide preliminary decree dated 21.06.1988 and sub-sequently made the decree final on 12.03.1990 as per report of the Advocate Commissioner. Then the plaintiff filed Execution Case No.07 of 1990 and obtained delivery of possession on 07.04.1990 and thus the partition suit was finally disposed of. 

 6. After disposal of the partition suit, the defendant no.1 including the petitioner herein filed an application under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting aside the decree in the partition suit. Upon hearing the parties, learned Assistant Judge set-aside the decree passed in the partition suit vide order dated 16.06, 1990 and thereby restored Other Suit No.28 of 1959 in its original file and number subject to payment 6f the cost of Tk.500/- only, holding that from the record it transpires that after arrival of the record from the Higher Court the parties were not informed, that the suit was not disposed of in accordance with the direction of the Higher Court and that order dated 23.05.1987 was not passed in accordance with law. 

 "The learned Advocate-on-record for the petitioner submits that the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division erred in not holding that availability of alternative remedy under other provisions of the Code does not always stand in the way of exercise of the inherent power of the Court for doing even handed justice for which alone the Court exists inasmuch as defendant no.7 Fazul Sheikh died on 08.02.1987 but the plaintiffs did not substitute the legal heirs of defendant no.1 and obtained preliminary decree on 21.06.1988 and final decree on 12,03.1990 in the absence of the heirs of the defendant no.1 without serving any notice upon them and the willful concealment of said fact tantamounts to practicing fraud upon the Court which is a good ground to invoke provision of section 151 C.P.C. for setting aside the ex-parte decree. The learned Advocate-on-record also submits that the learned Judge of the High Court: Division erred in not taking into consideration the principle of law laid down in the cases reported in 50 DLR 403, 42 DL R (AD) 74 and 49 DLR 347 in the matter of application of section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure. He lastly submits that the learned Judge of the High Court Division failed to notice the findings of the trial Court regarding non-compliance of the direction of the High Court: for causing service of notice upon the petitioner after arrival of the records from the High Court Division in the trial Court and the plaintiff by practicing fraud upon the Court and the defendant 110.1 which prevented the defendants from appearing before the Court to contest the case and thereby caused serious prejudice to the petitioner, as such the judgment and order of the High Court Division setting aside the order of trial Court occasioned failure of justice." 

 "On' examination of the lower court records in appears that from the date of receipt of the case record i.e. on 27.04.1985 to 12.031990 as many as 24 dates had gone but the defendants did not take any steps, it also transpires from the order sheet that on 03.02.1987 amended notices were duly served upon the defendants and thereafter, the suit proceeded with. But inspite of that none of the defendants appeared. It further appears that date of ex-parte hearing was fixed on 01.04.1987 but on that date and on the subsequent date i.e. on 16.04.1987 the court did not hear the suit ex-parte as there was no time to hear. On 23.05.1987 the suit was heard ex-parte. On 05.10.1987 an Advocate Commissioner was appointed and on 05.02.1990 Advocate Commissioner submitted his report. 02.03.1990 was fixed for filing objection to the Advocate Commissioner report if any but no objection was filed by any one. So it is evident that the allegation that no notice was served is found to be not correct and from 27.04.1985 to 12.03.1990 for about long six years no steps were taken by the defendants. But when the final decree was passed on 19.03.1990 the defendants on 16.04.1990 i.e. after 28 days came up with an application under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting aside the exparte decrees. This application appears to have been filed well within the statutory period of time but instead of resorting to proper remedy available to the defendants. Application under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure had been tiled when there was enough time and alternative efficacious remedy was available to them under the Code, which they did not avail oft' (Sic.) 

 14. It appears that the Court below set-aside the decree passed in the partition suit on an application under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure filed by the defendants.
